dates.altered: Remodelled by Robert Adam; the listed-building entry says 'remodelled by Robert Adam 1761-5. Interior - a few room retain early Georgian features, rest redecorated 1765-77.'
dates.note: THREE DATINGS OF THE ADAM CAMPAIGN AND NONE IS CHOSEN. The listed-building entry (1080308) says the remodelling is 1761-5 with the interiors redecorated 1765-77. The Wikipedia infobox says 'Rebuilt 1761-1765'. The node's own exemplar says 'Remodelled 1761-80'. All are recorded.

quotes.text: PRINCIPAL BUILDING Situated in the centre of the site, Osterley Park House (listed grade I) consists of red-brick wings of three storeys around a raised courtyard with a taller brick tower with stone quoins and ogee cap projecting at each outer corner.
quotes.page: Register of Parks and Gardens list entry 1000287, PRINCIPAL BUILDING paragraph

quotes.text: The courtyard is entered through a grand Ionic portico on the east side. The portico stands at the head of a flight of steps and provides an entrance to the state rooms on the first floor, this being on a level with the courtyard.
quotes.page: Register of Parks and Gardens list entry 1000287, PRINCIPAL BUILDING paragraph

quotes.text: On the west side of the house a curved double staircase leads down from a pedimented door in the first-floor gallery to the garden. The mansion overlooks the east lawn with views to the Middle Lake.
quotes.page: Register of Parks and Gardens list entry 1000287, PRINCIPAL BUILDING paragraph

quotes.text: To the north of the mansion is the red-brick stable block (listed grade I). Built around a three-sided courtyard, the two-storey building has attics and turrets in the two internal angles.
quotes.page: Register of Parks and Gardens list entry 1000287, DESCRIPTION, stable block

note: Tranche 3, English Baroque / Palladian / Adam cluster, 5 Sep 2026. THE PIANO NOBILE IS STATED AS A CONSEQUENCE OF THE COURTYARD, WHICH IS THE ONE PLANNING FACT IN THIS RECORD A GENERATOR COULD USE: the portico 'provides an entrance to the state rooms on the first floor, this being on a level with the courtyard' -- the principal floor is at courtyard level because Adam raised the courtyard, not because he raised the house. The Etruscan Dressing Room this node's exemplar names is in neither Historic England entry. Historic England serves the Details section hard-wrapped. Every run of whitespace in these quotes is the extractor's line wrap collapsed to one space; nothing else was changed, and a word broken across a wrap is left broken. No rights line for the list entry TEXT was read verbatim here, so no `rights_evidence` is recorded rather than a borrowed one.
